findings.title: Plain Error returned for an authorization failure
findings.body: `throw new Error(...)` becomes a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR in tRPC, not a 404 or 403. It will also be logged as a server error. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `"FORBIDDEN"` instead. The UI shows only a generic toast, so the client never sees the real cause.

findings.title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gating
findings.body: The handler instantiates the real `CalendarCacheRepository` directly, so the mock that returns `[]` when calendar-cache is disabled is never used here. The mock's `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is therefore dead code. Resolve the repository through the same factory or feature check the other callers use. The extra groupBy also now runs on every `connectedCalendars` call, for all users and all calendar types.

findings.title: No-op update on SelectedCalendar for an unused field
findings.body: `updateMany(..., {})` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` bump. It runs on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, even when the credential has no selected calendars. Nothing in this PR displays `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`; the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. The `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` selects added in `user.ts` and `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` are likewise unused. Remove them, or explain what reads them.

findings.title: Hard-coded en-US date format in a localized string
findings.body: `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale, and the timestamp is interpolated with `escapeValue: false`. Use the locale from `useLocale` (`i18n.language`) so non-English users see dates in their own format.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not refresh the displayed cache status
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()`, which is the parent's `onChanged`. This component never invalidates `connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation. If `onChanged` does not refetch, the menu keeps showing "Last updated" and the delete option for a cache that no longer exists. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` on success.

findings.title: Unrelated, macOS-only dev script and package.json change in this PR
findings.body: `sed -i ''` works only with BSD sed, and `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the current working directory. The script and the `dev:cron` change to `npx tsx` are unrelated to cache deletion. `cleanup` always exits 0, so the failure paths (lines 49 and 58) report success. Move these to a separate PR or fix them.

contracts.action: Delete CalendarCache rows for a credential
contracts.before_after: The handler checks that the credential belongs to ctx.user.id immediately before deleting, so the target is verified. The deleteMany is scoped to that one credentialId. It does not use the repository method.
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast and parent onChanged. The cache status in the menu may stay stale unless onChanged refetches.
contracts.failure_mode: A non-owner gets a plain Error, which tRPC returns as a 500, and the UI shows a generic error toast. Nothing is deleted. Cache rows are re-creatable, so the delete is low-risk.

summary: The feature works as described, but it has a few rough edges. The delete handler throws a plain Error, which tRPC turns into a 500. The cache-status query bypasses the calendar-cache mock. The UI hard-codes the en-US date format and does not invalidate its own data after a cache delete. The SelectedCalendar `updatedAt` bump looks unused. The tunnel script and the `dev:cron` change are unrelated to this PR. The delete itself re-verifies credential ownership right before deleting, so I found no data-safety defect.
